/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 17 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2567 (44)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4128 (102)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1975 (5)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1415 (17)
Baltic Handysize Index: 741 (11)
CAPESIZE
The closed the week on a firmer footing, with the BCI 182 5TC advancing by $920 to settle at $37,435, capping a period of sustained strength across both basins. Gains were supported by incremental improvements, with C5 rising by $0.315 to $13.595 and C3 up by $0.296 to $32.673. In the Pacific, the market ended the week on a positive note, with rates nudging higher despite some early resistance. Offers for C5 began the day around $14.00, though fixtures were concluded at $13.60 by a major, with some indications suggesting fixtures slightly below $13.50. Two miners were active, helping underpin sentiment and maintain a firm floor to the market. Across the Atlantic, the underlying tone remained constructive, with fundamentals continuing to provide support. While the North Atlantic saw a more subdued finish following recent gains, there was still evidence of strengthening demand, with C3 bids reportedly edging closer to $33. On the period front, Classic is reported to have fixed the Moundreas controlled NN Tenacity (179,929 2011) delivery Huanghua 22/25 April for 12 months timecharter at $30,500.
PANAMAX
Today saw more gains across the vast majority of routes with positive sentiment echoed across the basins. With that said, it did have a Friday feel as some market participants took a breath in order to see what the new week brings. In the Atlantic we are still hearing about a price differential between grains and minerals trades although there were a number of reported fixtures and the P1A increased by $146 to conclude the week at $14,416. Fronthaul is also following this same positive trend line with activity evident. In Asia, Indonesia is still active especially for trades into India and Southeast Asia as is Australia which in turn is having a knock-on effect on the P4 which increased today by $101. Reported period activity today was muted whilst the P5TC grew by $43 to bring the week to a close at $17,773.

Atlantic
The Sea fighter (81,856 2018) was reported to be coming open Santos 24/28 April although others have said Itaqui was said to have fixed a trip to Skaw-Gibraltar at $30,500 to Messrs Bunge.

Asia
Shine Coral (82,352 2024) open in Qinzhou 23/25 April was said to have fixed a trip at $22,000 from Indonesia to India with some saying the charterer, Libra, have a load option out of Australia. The scrubber fitted Bulk Malaysia (95,639 2014) open Shanghai 14/16 May fixed a trip via East Coast Australia to Japan with coal at $19,000 to Daiichi although it is unknown how the scrubber benefit was split. The scrubber fitted Ultra Cougar (81,922 2015) open in Hong Kong 23 April and the GCL Icon (82,567 2021) Zhoushan 24-25 April were both said to have been placed on subjects, but further details lacked. The Milagro (75,205 2009), which is also scrubber fitted, open in Dangjin 17/18 April was reported as fixed but more clarity was lacking. Messrs ASL covered on subjects their North Pacific to China stem for 5 May onwards and Classic also placed on subjects their Indonesia into Bangladesh coal stem for 22-28 April dates.
SUPRAMAX
A positive end to the week with most areas remaining in positive territory. Brokers saying that demand remained both in the Atlantic and Asian arenas. Ther was talk of further period action, the ZY Ningbo (63,789 2025) open Fangcheng fixed for 4/6 months trading with the first leg understood to be clinker to West Africa at $19,750, but no more details came to light. The 11TC average finished the week up $217 at $17,886.

Atlantic
The Sorsi (64,043 2017) open Veracruz 19 April was heard to have fixed at $28,000 for a trip delivery SW Pass redelivery North Continent with coal with coal to Starbulk, but some said it was closer to $27,500. The Ariadni (63,155 2014) open Brownsville prompt fixed basis delivery Pascagoula with petcoke to Italy at $31,000 with Pangaea. Elsewhere, the CMB Teniers (63,667 2021) open Tema 15/20 April was linked to Reachy covering a vessel for a trip redelivery China with agriproducts at $17,250 plus $725,000 ballast bonus. The SSI Impressive (63,500 2026) open Conakry 24/28 April was heard to have been placed on subjects basis delivery Recalada for a trip redelivery China with agricultural products at $17,750 plus $775,000 ballast bonus. The Pacific Archer (52,407 2001) was rumoured fixed basis Conakry via Vitoria redelivery China with lithium ore at $14,000, but no more details came to light.

Asia
The SSI Interceptor (63,896 2023) open Gresik 23/27 April was heard to have been placed on subjects redelivery WC India at $27,000 with coal to Transpower. The Vosco Sky (52,523 2001) open Singapore 19 April was heard fixed for a trip via Indonesia redelivery SE Asia at $12,500. Further north, the Yangtze Brightness (57,021 2010) open Ningde 19 April fixed via China redelivery South Africa at $18,000.

HANDYSIZE
A typical Friday with limited fresh fixing information surfacing and despite this it was a fairly positive end to the week overall for the sector. The Continent- Mediterranean gained a little momentum although brokers said it still remained finely balanced. Both the US Gulf and South Atlantic again saw green shoots but as said actual fixing remained sparce. The uptick seen recently continued from the Asian arena as brokers broker a slight tightening of prompt vessels and better levels of enquiry. The Iron Maiden (36,372 2014) open Panjin 18/24 April was heard fixed for a trip redelivery EC India at $15,000. The 7TC average finished the week up $194 at $13,337.

Market Fundamentals
US Weekly Grain Exports

In the week to 9 April, US combined exports of corn, wheat, soy (beans and meal) and sorghum dipped 0.1 Mt from the prior week to 3.2 Mt, USDA data show. Corn exports declined 0.3 Mt on the week to 1.6 Mt, while wheat shipments eased 0.1 Mt to 0.3 Mt. Conversely, shipments of soy (beans+meal) and sorghums each lifted 0.1 Mt to a respective 1.2 Mt and 0.2 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Another volatile day in the Cape FFA market with Apr and May paid up to highs of 32500 and 35000 respectively. The June range was wide also 33200-34250 while the May v Jun continues to widen and strengthen up to +700. Q2 traded in huge volume up to 33850 during the rally, while activity on the Q3 stalled, trading between 30800 and 31500. The Q3 v Q4 was legged at +100 early in the day with the range on Q4 alone was 30600-30850. Similar to the Q4, the Cals were relatively stable, with 25800-26000 C27 and 23000-23150 C28.

PMX
Pmx had a quiet start to the day before an afternoon flurry off the back of some macro uncertainty, leaving May trading to highs of 19500. We did find a ceiling and steadily traded back down to just above opening levels. while Jun held a narrow range of 19100 to 19500. Further out, Q3 traded at a low of 18450 and was paid up to 18800, finishing around 18600, while Q4 traded around 17000 and saw some late improvement to 17250. Cal 27 traded around 15000. Overall, it was a steady end to the week, with the market holding firm despite weakness in the wider energy complex.

SMX + HANDY
The SMX market was once again rangebound trading around previous days levels, with a firm floor in place as buyers were prevalent throughout the day. Apr sentiment appeared very positive with the contract trading up to a high of 15700 (BOM 17186, Spot 15852). May traded from 16800 – 17150, Jun 16700 – 17200 and Q2 was steady between 16300 – 16350. Q3 traded 15800 – 16250, with the bulk of activity around 16000 and Q4 traded 14850 – 15200. Cal27 also trended higher, trading 12900 – 13000.

Carbon
EUA Futures advanced this morning on optimism that a Middle East peace deal could be reached, and climbed further as news broke in the afternoon that Iran would permit safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Overall, the carbon market increased 3.4% on close-to-average volumes, with the benchmark Dec26 contract trading at �77.51/eua, up �2.55.

Simultaneously, regional energy prices declined sharply, with the prompt month TTF falling into the high �38/MWh range and the prospect of energy demand destruction has materially decreased.

PAC: Firming         ATL: Very Tight
Market Comments
Some Friday resistance found in the Paciﬁc today, as two Hedland majors
each took a handful of vessels. Peripheral demand still robust and
operator C5 interest high. Targeting early split dates and early May, one
Hedland major wasted little time and took a handful of vessels at $13.60-
70 C5 range. The other present Hedland major reportedly ﬁxed a couple
stems around $13.45-50 and were trying another. Come Friday, many
pondered when the last time they saw a ballaster list this short was. Not
wanting to be left behind, operators engaged early ﬁxing at $32.88 for
mid May and comfortably breaking the $33 mark at $33.50 was done.
Plenty demand remains for May dates and has teed up what can only be
another exciting week next week. Despite dominating the cargo book,
fronthaul concluded activity was proven relatively light as the week ended.
Fundamentals remained strongly in favour of owners, as an Egyptian end-
user tendered their Narvik to Egypt stem.

Capesize Report17th April 2026
Market Comments
An overall strong week in the Paciﬁc with volumes remaining strong whilst levels healthy keeping some owners in the Paciﬁc rather
than choosing to ballast. The Paciﬁc opened to a slow start to the week as Greek owners were absent for Orthodox Easter. Those
owners present set the tone early on with oﬀers in the region of $13. Two majors did come to market, however neither ended up
bidding and rolled their stems into the next day despite levels in the region of $12.65 being oﬀered to the Dampier major. Tuesday
saw activity spike with the return of Greek owners, as levels of $13 were oﬀered from the get-go. The Dampier major was quick to
ﬁx a couple C5 stems at $12.80 for 28/30 April and 29 April/01 May. Two Hedland majors shortly followed suit, ﬁxing their C5 stems
for similar dates at $13. It was also reported that one operator secured their cargo out of Hedland to China at $13.30 for 27/29 April.
Additionally, the usual major out of TRMT ﬁxed their stem for 22/24 April at high $8.00’s for a trip to Bohadopi. Also, an East
Australia cargo to China was agreed in the high $17s for 01/10 May. The market - fuelled with conﬁdence - spurred oﬀers to stand at
$14 early on Wednesday. A handful of C5 stems were soon agreed by two majors out of Dampier Hedland for split April and early
May dates levels in the range of $13.40 to $13.50. Strong levels were seen midweek as owners continued to set the tone with oﬀers
in the region of high $13s to $14 until soon after the Dampier major ﬁxed a handful of C5 stems for 1/3 May and 2/4 May dates at
$13.25, as well as one Hedland major ﬁxing their cargo at $13.20 for similar dates. All in all, the later half of the week held continued
strength in demand as focus now looked towards early May cargoes with tighter April dates no longer sought after. Into Friday,
resistance was found in the Paciﬁc today, as two Hedland majors each took a handful of vessels. Peripheral demand was robust and
operator C5 interest high. Targeting early split dates and early May, one Hedland major wasted little time and took a handful of
vessels at $13.60-70 C5 range. The other present Hedland major reportedly ﬁxed a couple stems around $13.45-50.
Another seismic week in the South Atlantic as the basin added over $2.50 to C3. Volumes in the latter half of last week cleared out a
notable chunk of ballasters, whilst Monday welcomed a healthy inﬂow of cargo. With plenty to cover, two operators cracked on
ﬁxing at low-mid $31’s for early and mid May. Poised for action, the South erupted on Tuesday with well over double digit number
of ﬁxtures done. With early to mid May undeniably tight, operators bid the basin early, chasing primarily the modern standards that
remained. Rates initially concluded at $31 C3, before peaking at $32 a few times for the day. Into the middle of the week the South
impressively replenished again the battered cargo book. Building upon the previous day but tilting focus to mid and end May, saw
several vessels concluded at rates ranging between $32.50 - $32.80 C3, other than one sharper outlier at $32 for mid-May.
Standards remained the clear preference and were what was ﬁxed on the aforementioned, while the usual shipper out Itaguai ﬁxed
a Nuke at around mid $32.00’s C3. Into the latter half of the week, ballasters available for ﬁrst half May were scarce. Momentum
carried through Thursday, yet operators were less eager to chase the oﬀer. A TC ﬁxture concluded for a Brazil round voyage at
$40,000 + GBB of $450,000. Come Frida, many pondered when the last time they saw a ballaster list this short was. Not wanting to
be left beind, operators engaged early ﬁxing at $32.88 for mid May and comfortably breaking the $33 mark at $33.50 was done.
Plenty demand remains for May dates and has teed up what can only be another exciting week next week.
Already thin April tonnage posed as the vice whose grip continued to tighten as transatlantic stems readily ﬂowed into the North. It
was however, fronthaul business that ignited the week’s excitement. From Gibraltar, a vessel was ﬁxed for an end-users stem out of
Kamsar at $28 for 03-09 May. This ran to mid-high $60k’s basis C9, using $275k India positioning value. In addition, a transatlantic
cargo out of West Africa to Arzew ﬁxed at $8.40 for 01-10 May which as a Gibraltar round voyage ran to around mid $32,000. Still
undermarked, the C8 broke comfortably above $35,000 mid-week as a trio of stems were ﬁxed. First, an operator ﬁxing a vessel for
Baltimore stem back to the continent at $35,888. Later on a Narvik to Erdemir stem tendered and ﬁxed for split dates at $18.10,
breaking into the $38,000’s for redelivery Gibraltar. A German Steel Mill reportedly ﬁxed at similar TC equivalent levels, for their
Sept-Iles to Rotterdam cargo at high $12.00’s. Focus shifted to fronthaul business, after an active start to the week. A trader's fresh
stem from Canada to China for 05 May due to come to market as well as a Narvik to China cargo for split dates while in the
afternoon 07-13 May dates from Port Cartier to Qingdao. Despite dominating the cargo book, fronthaul concluded activity was
relatively light. Fundamentals remained strongly in favour of owners, as an Egyptian end-user tendered their Narvik to Egypt stem.

Handysize/Supramax Report17th April 2026
63,500 Atlantic: FIRMER      Paciﬁc: FIRMER           38,000 Atlantic: FIRMER      Paciﬁc: FIRMER
Atlantic Comment
The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) reached a 17-week high this week, surging past 2,354 points by Thursday
as the market beneﬁted from a strong pre-May cargo push. The rally was led by a 4.6% jump in
Capesize rates, with daily earnings climbing toward $26,000 as major miners in both the Atlantic
and Paciﬁc aggressively booked tonnage. However, bunker volatility remains a persistent challenge;
while Brent crude prices dipped mid-week to roughly $95 per barrel, marine fuel costs remain
historically elevated, forcing shipowners to maintain high voyage rates just to cover their soaring
operating expenses.
On the Continent, the market has begun to ﬁnd some footing this week, with activity gradually
picking up following the Easter period and sentiment showing signs of improvement. On the
Handysize market, rates have remained ﬁrm through the week, supported by a relatively tighter
tonnage list, with owners holding their ideas. There has been a slight increase in scrap cargoes,
which could begin to draw vessels away from grain trades, although this has yet to have a
noticeable impact. We have seen a 38,000 deadweight vessel rate a trip to West Africa at USD
16,500, representing an increase of around USD 2,500 compared to levels seen at the end of last
week. On the Supramax and Ultramax market activity remains quiet, with a slight pickup in
demand and early signs of tightening in the tonnage list. The overall balance remains comfortable,
though sentiment is beginning to turn more positive into the second half of April. We are seeing
Trans-Atlantic trips being rated at around USD 11,000, with a 61,000 deadweight vessel ﬁxing basis
Garrucha for redelivery in the USEC at USD 10,750 - in line with levels discussed earlier in the week
for similar routes.
The Mediterranean market remained ﬂat, with limited cargo failing to match the growing tonnage
list. On the Handysize market, it has been very quiet, with limited activity and few ﬁxtures coming
together. Charterers remain selective, while reduced opportunities in the Black Sea are pushing
some vessels to consider ballasting out to secure employment, adding further pressure on the
market. A similar environment is seen on the Supramax and Ultramax market, where a slight
pickup in West Mediterranean demand has not been enough to absorb the available tonnage.
Trans-Atlantic trips are being discussed in the USD 7,000–9,500 range across all sizes, in line with
levels at the start of the week, although rates have yet to be secured.
The East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market has surged this week, as a wave of fresh
demand in the south has eﬀectively wiped out prompt tonnage and driven rates sharply higher.
Transatlantic (TA) levels have jumped to the $20,000– $21,000 range, fueled by a robust grain book
across the Argentina and South Brazil range that has forced charterers to pay up as the vessel list
thins. This rally is also supported by an uptick in demand for front-haul trips, further tightening the
Atlantic supply. In contrast, the trade from ECSA towards the West Coast of South America (WCSA)
has remained notably quiet, with little fresh inquiry to match the heat seen on the Atlantic-bound
routes. The ECSA Supramax and Ultramax markets are ending the week on a slightly more healthy
footing, particularly regarding fronthaul demand. However, a persistent layer of spot tonnage
continues to linger in the region, largely due to a noticeable lack of fresh TA inquiries which has
prevented a more aggressive rally. For Ultramax units, current rate levels reﬂect this divide: trips
toward the Continent are currently fetching around $26,500, with a slight premium for
Mediterranean at $27,500. Longhaul business remains the most lucrative with ECSA to the Persian
Gulf-Japan range hovering at $17,250 + $725,000 Gross ballast bonus.
The US Gulf Handysize market felt ﬁrmer this week, with sentiment improving in line with the
stronger dry bulk indices. Owners were testing higher ideas, but in reality there wasn’t much fresh
cargo to back it up, and ﬁxture evidence remained limited. Overall, the move feels more sentiment-
driven than fundamentally supported. The April tonnage list is still on the long side, but it looks
more evenly positioned compared to previous weeks, which gives the market a more balanced feel.
This has been enough to let owners hold their ground despite the lack of new enquiry. Activity
slowed towards the end of the week, with Friday feeling very quiet. The market remains cautious
given the geopolitical uncertainty in around the Strait of Hormuz and how this could impact the
wider market. Overall, sentiment remains positive, supported by gradual improvements in the
wider dry bulk market, although the lack of cargo visibility and suﬃcient vessel supply may limit
further upside in the near term. On the Supramax and Ultramax market in the US Gulf, an increase
in end-April enquiry has driven a stronger push in rates midweek, with a number of Trans-Atlantic
cargoes entering the market. We have seen an Ultramax ﬁx a premium petcoke cargo from the US
Gulf to Italy at USD 31,000, marking the top of the market. Fronthaul business has also ﬁrmed, with
levels climbing into the mid USD 20,000s.

Handysize/Supramax Report17th April 2026
Paciﬁc Comments
This week, the Paciﬁc Supramax market continued to exhibit a ﬁrm and upward-trending pattern, with fundamentals showing further improvement compared to the previous
period. Supported particularly by the strengthening period market, the overall earnings level has moved up noticeably. Coal shipments have increased, regional trading activity has
picked up, and the seasonal start of nickel ore exports has provided additional momentum. At the same time, temporary tightness in tonnage supply on certain routes has pushed
both backhaul (BH) and regional freight rates higher to varying degrees.
The Indonesian coal sector saw a phase of recovery this week, with a moderate increase in fresh cargoes entering the market. The Indo/SE Asia route remained ﬁrm, with ﬁxtures
reported such as an SMX open KSC ﬁxing around USD 14k for Indo/Thai, and another SMX open Singapore achieving up to USD 16.5k. Demand on the Indo/China route remained
relatively limited; however, supported by the overall stronger market, SMX delivery Singapore ﬁxing levels were still maintained around USD 16–17k. The Indo/India (WCI) route
showed the most pronounced gains this week, with rates rising signiﬁcantly. Market indications include a UMX delivery Singapore ﬁxing at USD 23.5k for Indo/WCI, as well as a
UMX open Cai Mep ﬁxing at USD 25k for Indo/Bdesh, reﬂecting strong demand from the Indian subcontinent.
The North Vietnam/South China region continued to serve as a key pillar of support for the market, with trading activity remaining at a high level. Clinker exports from Vietnam to
Bangladesh stayed active, with rates further strengthening, including a reported UMX open South China ﬁxing at USD 25k. Meanwhile, with the onset of the nickel ore season,
activity in related trades has increased, with ﬁxtures such as an SMX open Xiamen ﬁxing around USD 18k for nickel ore to China, as well as an SMX open Singapore ﬁxing at similar
levels.
The NOPAC market remained stable overall, though with relatively limited trading activity. A UMX open Japan ﬁxing around USD 18k for a NOPAC round voyage was reported,
indicating stable rate levels and providing a ﬂoor for the broader market.
North China steel and general cargo exports strengthened signiﬁcantly this week, particularly on routes to the Red Sea and Mediterranean. Reported ﬁxtures include an SMX open
North China ﬁxing around USD 19k to the Red Sea, and a UMX open CJK ﬁxing around USD 23k to the Black Sea via Goa, highlighting strong demand for long-haul voyages. Bulk
cargoes also provided support, with an SMX open Japan ﬁxing at USD 16.5k for a trip to Bangladesh carrying slag, maintaining a ﬁrm tone overall.
The Australian market also remained ﬁrm this week, with stable cargo ﬂow from supply-side regions. Grain and salt from Western Australia, coal from Eastern Australia, and
minerals from Northern Australia continued to generate steady demand, supporting the regional market and contributing to an upward shift in freight levels.
In the period market, strength persisted throughout the week. Supported by the rising spot market and ﬁrm FFA levels, period rates continued to climb. UMX short period ﬁxtures
were commonly concluded at USD 19k–19.5k, while one-year period rates increased to USD 18k–18.5k+, reﬂecting strong owner conﬁdence in the near- to mid-term outlook.
Overall, the Paciﬁc Supramax market this week demonstrated a steady yet ﬁrm upward trajectory, driven by both improving fundamentals and ongoing macro uncertainties. With
continued cargo ﬂow, seasonal demand support, and ﬁrm owner sentiment, the market is expected to remain ﬁrm in the short term, with potential for further upside. However,
attention should still be paid to macroeconomic developments and the potential return of tonnage, which may impact the pace of the market going forward.

IN THE NOPAC MARKET, THE WEEK BEGAN ON A QUIETER NOTE WITH LIMITED GRAIN ENQUIRY, AND ALTHOUGH ACTIVITY REMAINED STEADY, IT
NEVER BECAME A KEY DRIVER FOR THE PACIFIC. MIDWEEK SAW SOME STABILITY WITH GRAINS HOLDING AT REASONABLE LEVELS, BUT THE SECTOR
LACKED MOMENTUM COMPARED TO THE MINERALS DRIVEN SOUTHERN MARKETS. BY THE END OF THE WEEK, THERE WAS A SLIGHT UPTICK IN
GRAIN INTEREST, THOUGH OVERALL SENTIMENT REMAINED MORE SUBDUED, WITH A SMALL DROP IN AVAILABLE TONNAGE HELPING TO KEEP
RATES SUPPORTED DESPITE LIMITED CARGO GROWTH.
THE AUSSIE MARKET WAS A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR TO THE WEEK’S STRENGTH, PARTICULARLY THROUGH MIDWEEK WHERE STRONG COAL ENQUIRY
INCLUDING JAPANESE TENDERS AND CHINESE DEMAND KEPT PRESSURE ON RATES AND PUSHED FIXTURES HIGHER. HOWEVER, AFTER A BUSY
PERIOD, ACTIVITY BEGAN TO TAPER OFF FROM THURSDAY ONWARDS, WITH A NOTICEABLE REDUCTION IN FRESH SPOT DEMAND AND A SHIFT
TOWARDS MORE FORWARD DATED CARGOES. BY FRIDAY, EAST AUS COAL, THE KEY DRIVER EARLIER IN THE WEEK, HAD SOFTENED, CONTRIBUTING
TO THE OVERALL SLOWDOWN IN RATE MOMENTUM, EVEN AS LEVELS REMAINED ELEVATED.
THE INDO MARKET REMAINED CONSISTENTLY ACTIVE THROUGHOUT THE WEEK AND WAS A KEY PILLAR OF SUPPORT FOR THE PACIFIC. STRONG

AMONG CHARTERERS, PARTICULARLY MIDWEEK WHEN SOME SPOT CARGOES INTO INDIA PAID UP AND OWNERS PUSHED OFFERS HIGHER. EVEN

Market Fundamentals
US Weekly Grain Exports
In the week to 9 April, US combined exports of corn, wheat,
soy (beans and meal) and sorghum dipped 0.1 Mt from the
prior week to 3.2 Mt, USDA data show. Corn exports declined
0.3 Mt on the week to 1.6 Mt, while wheat shipments eased
0.1 Mt to 0.3 Mt. Conversely, shipments of soy (beans+meal)
and sorghums each lifted 0.1 Mt to a respective 1.2 Mt and
0.2 Mt.
Trading Commentary
Cape
Another volatile day in the Cape FFA market with Apr and
May paid up to highs of 32500 and 35000 respectively. The
June range was wide also 33200-34250 while the May v Jun
continues to widen and strengthen up to +700. Q2 traded in
huge volume up to 33850 during the rally, while activity on
the Q3 stalled, trading between 30800 and 31500. The Q3 v
Q4 was legged at +100 early in the day with the range on Q4
alone was 30600-30850. Similar to the Q4, the Cals were
relatively stable, with 25800-26000 C27 and 23000-23150
C28.
PMX
Pmx had a quiet start to the day before an afternoon ﬂurry
oﬀ the back of some macro uncertainty, leaving May trading
to highs of 19500. We did ﬁnd a ceiling and steadily traded
back down to just above opening levels. while Jun held a
narrow range of 19100 to 19500. Further out, Q3 traded at a
low of 18450 and was paid up to 18800, ﬁnishing around
18600, while Q4 traded around 17000 and saw some late
improvement to 17250. Cal 27 traded around 15000. Overall,
it was a steady end to the week, with the market holding ﬁrm
despite weakness in the wider energy complex.
SMX + HANDY

previous days levels, with a ﬁrm ﬂoor in place as buyers were
prevalent throughout the day. Apr sentiment appeared very

16700 – 17200 and Q2 was steady between 16300 – 16350.

There has been a distinct improvement in the volume of enquiry from all the major recycling desti-
nations over the past week, which has translated into a notable increase in concluded sales.

India has been the primary beneficiary, securing several chemical tanker sales, including one
concluded on private terms, all with high quantities of solid stainless steel. When combined with
bunkers ROB included in the transactions, these units have generated exceptionally strong price
levels.

Stolt Tankers have sold the “Stolt Cedar” (11,436 lwt) at a reported level of USD 910 per lwt, and
the “Stolt Sea” (8,074 lwt) at a slightly lower level of USD 850 per lwt. Both vessels are understood
to contain significant, albeit undisclosed, quantities of stainless steel, and have already arrived,
with beaching expected during the upcoming high tides.

Sinokor have now concluded the long -anticipated sale of the gas carrier “Hongkong Ener-
gy” (31,340 lwt) at a reported level of USD 510 per lwt, on an as is basis in Malaysia. Given the
vessel’s extended lay -up history, it is understood that Buyers will proceed with towage rather than
reactivation for the delivery voyage, with Bangladesh anticipated to be the final recycling destina-
tion.

More broadly, domestic steel demand has strengthened across all major markets, providing further
support to improving price levels from the waterfront. This firmer demand backdrop, combined with
the increasing number of HKC -approved recycling yards, is beginning to add real momentum to
competition within the sector, effectively giving the market a much -needed breath of fresh air after
a prolonged period of subdued activity.

However, despite the recent increase in concluded sales, the overall supply of tonnage remains
insufficient to satisfy the full breadth of demand. This is particularly relevant given the number of
yards that have invested heavily to achieve HKC compliance, all of whom are now actively seeking
to secure units. As such, while competition has clearly intensified, the challenge will be ensuring a
consistent flow of candidates to keep all end users engaged in what is becoming an increasingly
competitive and capacity -rich market.

items.parsed_text: Capesize Report17th April 2026 PAC: Firming ATL: Very Tight Market Comments Some Friday resistance found in the Pacific today, as two Hedland majors each took a handful of vessels. Peripheral demand still robust and operator C5 interest high. Targeting early split dates and early May, one Hedland major wasted little time and took a handful of vessels at $13.60- 70 C5 range. The other present Hedland major reportedly fixed a couple stems around $13.45-50 and were trying another. Come Friday, many pondered when the last time they saw a ballaster list this short was. Not wanting to be left behind, operators engaged early fixing at $32.88 for mid May and comfortably breaking the $33 mark at $33.50 was done. Plenty demand remains for May dates and has teed up what can only be another exciting week next week. Despite dominating the cargo book, fronthaul concluded activity was proven relatively light as the week ended. Fundamentals remained strongly in favour of owners, as an Egyptian end- user tendered their Narvik to Egypt stem. The Pacific opened to a slow start to the week as Greek owners were absent for Orthodox Easter. Those owners present set the tone early on with offers in the region of $13. Two majors did come to market, however neither ended up bidding and rolled their stems into the next day despite levels in the region of $12.65 being offered to the Dampier major. Tuesday saw activity spike with the return of Greek owners, as levels of $13 were offered from the get-go. The Dampier major was quick to fix a couple C5 stems at $12.80 for 28/30 April and 29 April/01 May. Two Hedland majors shortly followed suit, fixing their C5 stems for similar dates at $13. It was also reported that one operator secured their cargo out of Hedland to China at $13.30 for 27/29 April. Additionally, the usual major out of TRMT fixed their stem for 22/24 April at high $8.00’s for a trip to Bohadopi. Also, an East Australia cargo to China was agreed in the high $17s for 01/10 May. The market - fuelled with confidence - spurred offers to stand at $14 early on Wednesday. A handful of C5 stems were soon agreed by two majors out of Dampier Hedland for split April and early May dates levels in the range of $13.40 to $13.50. Strong levels were seen midweek as owners continued to set the tone with offers in the region of high $13s to $14 until soon after the Dampier major fixed a handful of C5 stems for 1/3 May and 2/4 May dates at $13.25, as well as one Hedland major fixing their cargo at $13.20 for similar dates. All in all, the later half of the week held continued strength in demand as focus now looked towards early May cargoes with tighter April dates no longer sought after. Into Friday, resistance was found in the Pacific today, as two Hedland majors each took a handful of vessels. Peripheral demand was robust and operator C5 interest high. Targeting early split dates and early May, one Hedland major wasted little time and took a handful of vessels at $13.60-70 C5 range. The other present Hedland major reportedly fixed a couple stems around $13.45-50. Another seismic week in the South Atlantic as the basin added over $2.50 to C3. Volumes in the latter half of last week cleared out a notable chunk of ballasters, whilst Monday welcomed a healthy inflow of cargo. With plenty to cover, two operators cracked on fixing at low-mid $31’s for early and mid May. Poised for action, the South erupted on Tuesday with well over double digit number of fixtures done. With early to mid May undeniably tight, operators bid the basin early, chasing primarily the modern standards that remained. Rates initially concluded at $31 C3, before peaking at $32 a few times for the day. Into the middle of the week the South impressively replenished again the battered cargo book. Building upon the previous day but tilting focus to mid and end May, saw several vessels concluded at rates ranging between $32.50 - $32.80 C3, other than one sharper outlier at $32 for mid-May. Standards remained the clear preference and were what was fixed on the aforementioned, while the usual shipper out Itaguai fixed a Nuke at around mid $32.00’s C3. Into the latter half of the week, ballasters available for first half May were scarce. Momentum carried through Thursday, yet operators were less eager to chase the offer. A TC fixture concluded for a Brazil round voyage at $40,000 + GBB of $450,000. Come Frida, many pondered when the last time they saw a ballaster list this short was. Not wanting to be left beind, operators engaged early fixing at $32.88 for mid May and comfortably breaking the $33 mark at $33.50 was done. Plenty demand remains for May dates and has teed up what can only be another exciting week next week. Already thin April tonnage posed as the vice whose grip continued to tighten as transatlantic stems readily flowed into the North. It was however, fronthaul business that ignited the week’s excitement. From Gibraltar, a vessel was fixed for an end-users stem out of Kamsar at $28 for 03-09 May. This ran to mid-high $60k’s basis C9, using $275k India positioning value. In addition, a transatlantic cargo out of West Africa to Arzew fixed at $8.40 for 01-10 May which as a Gibraltar round voyage ran to around mid $32,000. Still undermarked, the C8 broke comfortably above $35,000 mid-week as a trio of stems were fixed. First, an operator fixing a vessel for Baltimore stem back to the continent at $35,888. Later on a Narvik to Erdemir stem tendered and fixed for split dates at $18.10, breaking into the $38,000’s for redelivery Gibraltar. A German Steel Mill reportedly fixed at similar TC equivalent levels, for their Sept-Iles to Rotterdam cargo at high $12.00’s. Focus shifted to fronthaul business, after an active start to the week. A trader's fresh stem from Canada to China for 05 May due to come to market as well as a Narvik to China cargo for split dates while in the afternoon 07-13 May dates from Port Cartier to Qingdao. Despite dominating the cargo book, fronthaul concluded activity was relatively light. Fundamentals remained strongly in favour of owners, as an Egyptian end-user tendered their Narvik to Egypt stem. items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report17th April 2026 63,500 Atlantic: FIRMER Pacific: FIRMER 38,000 Atlantic: FIRMER Pacific: FIRMER Atlantic Comment The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) reached a 17-week high this week, surging past 2,354 points by Thursday as the market benefited from a strong pre-May cargo push. The rally was led by a 4.6% jump in Capesize rates, with daily earnings climbing toward $26,000 as major miners in both the Atlantic and Pacific aggressively booked tonnage. However, bunker volatility remains a persistent challenge; while Brent crude prices dipped mid-week to roughly $95 per barrel, marine fuel costs remain historically elevated, forcing shipowners to maintain high voyage rates just to cover their soaring operating expenses. On the Continent, the market has begun to find some footing this week, with activity gradually picking up following the Easter period and sentiment showing signs of improvement. On the Handysize market, rates have remained firm through the week, supported by a relatively tighter tonnage list, with owners holding their ideas. There has been a slight increase in scrap cargoes, which could begin to draw vessels away from grain trades, although this has yet to have a noticeable impact. We have seen a 38,000 deadweight vessel rate a trip to West Africa at USD 16,500, representing an increase of around USD 2,500 compared to levels seen at the end of last week. On the Supramax and Ultramax market activity remains quiet, with a slight pickup in demand and early signs of tightening in the tonnage list. The overall balance remains comfortable, though sentiment is beginning to turn more positive into the second half of April. We are seeing Trans-Atlantic trips being rated at around USD 11,000, with a 61,000 deadweight vessel fixing basis Garrucha for redelivery in the USEC at USD 10,750 - in line with levels discussed earlier in the week for similar routes. The Mediterranean market remained flat, with limited cargo failing to match the growing tonnage list. On the Handysize market, it has been very quiet, with limited activity and few fixtures coming together. Charterers remain selective, while reduced opportunities in the Black Sea are pushing some vessels to consider ballasting out to secure employment, adding further pressure on the market. A similar environment is seen on the Supramax and Ultramax market, where a slight pickup in West Mediterranean demand has not been enough to absorb the available tonnage. Trans-Atlantic trips are being discussed in the USD 7,000–9,500 range across all sizes, in line with levels at the start of the week, although rates have yet to be secured. The East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market has surged this week, as a wave of fresh demand in the south has effectively wiped out prompt tonnage and driven rates sharply higher. Transatlantic (TA) levels have jumped to the $20,000– $21,000 range, fueled by a robust grain book across the Argentina and South Brazil range that has forced charterers to pay up as the vessel list thins. This rally is also supported by an uptick in demand for front-haul trips, further tightening the Atlantic supply. In contrast, the trade from ECSA towards the West Coast of South America (WCSA) has remained notably quiet, with little fresh inquiry to match the heat seen on the Atlantic-bound routes. The ECSA Supramax and Ultramax markets are ending the week on a slightly more healthy footing, particularly regarding fronthaul demand. However, a persistent layer of spot tonnage continues to linger in the region, largely due to a noticeable lack of fresh TA inquiries which has prevented a more aggressive rally. For Ultramax units, current rate levels reflect this divide: trips toward the Continent are currently fetching around $26,500, with a slight premium for Mediterranean at $27,500. Longhaul business remains the most lucrative with ECSA to the Persian Gulf-Japan range hovering at $17,250 + $725,000 Gross ballast bonus. The US Gulf Handysize market felt firmer this week, with sentiment improving in line with the stronger dry bulk indices. Owners were testing higher ideas, but in reality there wasn’t much fresh cargo to back it up, and fixture evidence remained limited. Overall, the move feels more sentiment- driven than fundamentally supported. The April tonnage list is still on the long side, but it looks more evenly positioned compared to previous weeks, which gives the market a more balanced feel. This has been enough to let owners hold their ground despite the lack of new enquiry. Activity slowed towards the end of the week, with Friday feeling very quiet. The market remains cautious given the geopolitical uncertainty in around the Strait of Hormuz and how this could impact the wider market. Overall, sentiment remains positive, supported by gradual improvements in the wider dry bulk market, although the lack of cargo visibility and suﬃcient vessel supply may limit further upside in the near term. On the Supramax and Ultramax market in the US Gulf, an increase in end-April enquiry has driven a stronger push in rates midweek, with a number of Trans-Atlantic cargoes entering the market. We have seen an Ultramax fix a premium petcoke cargo from the US Gulf to Italy at USD 31,000, marking the top of the market. Fronthaul business has also firmed, with levels climbing into the mid USD 20,000s. Supported particularly by the strengthening period market, the overall earnings level has moved up noticeably. Coal shipments have increased, regional trading activity has picked up, and the seasonal start of nickel ore exports has provided additional momentum. At the same time, temporary tightness in tonnage supply on certain routes has pushed both backhaul (BH) and regional freight rates higher to varying degrees. The Indonesian coal sector saw a phase of recovery this week, with a moderate increase in fresh cargoes entering the market. The Indo/SE Asia route remained firm, with fixtures reported such as an SMX open KSC fixing around USD 14k for Indo/Thai, and another SMX open Singapore achieving up to USD 16.5k. Demand on the Indo/China route remained relatively limited; however, supported by the overall stronger market, SMX delivery Singapore fixing levels were still maintained around USD 16–17k. The Indo/India (WCI) route showed the most pronounced gains this week, with rates rising significantly. Market indications include a UMX delivery Singapore fixing at USD 23.5k for Indo/WCI, as well as a UMX open Cai Mep fixing at USD 25k for Indo/Bdesh, reflecting strong demand from the Indian subcontinent. The North Vietnam/South China region continued to serve as a key pillar of support for the market, with trading activity remaining at a high level. Clinker exports from Vietnam to Bangladesh stayed active, with rates further strengthening, including a reported UMX open South China fixing at USD 25k. Meanwhile, with the onset of the nickel ore season, activity in related trades has increased, with fixtures such as an SMX open Xiamen fixing around USD 18k for nickel ore to China, as well as an SMX open Singapore fixing at similar levels. The NOPAC market remained stable overall, though with relatively limited trading activity. A UMX open Japan fixing around USD 18k for a NOPAC round voyage was reported, indicating stable rate levels and providing a floor for the broader market. North China steel and general cargo exports strengthened significantly this week, particularly on routes to the Red Sea and Mediterranean. Reported fixtures include an SMX open North China fixing around USD 19k to the Red Sea, and a UMX open CJK fixing around USD 23k to the Black Sea via Goa, highlighting strong demand for long-haul voyages. Bulk cargoes also provided support, with an SMX open Japan fixing at USD 16.5k for a trip to Bangladesh carrying slag, maintaining a firm tone overall. The Australian market also remained firm this week, with stable cargo flow from supply-side regions. Grain and salt from Western Australia, coal from Eastern Australia, and minerals from Northern Australia continued to generate steady demand, supporting the regional market and contributing to an upward shift in freight levels. In the period market, strength persisted throughout the week. Supported by the rising spot market and firm FFA levels, period rates continued to climb. UMX short period fixtures were commonly concluded at USD 19k–19.5k, while one-year period rates increased to USD 18k–18.5k+, reflecting strong owner confidence in the near- to mid-term outlook. Overall, the Pacific Supramax market this week demonstrated a steady yet firm upward trajectory, driven by both improving fundamentals and ongoing macro uncertainties. With continued cargo flow, seasonal demand support, and firm owner sentiment, the market is expected to remain firm in the short term, with potential for further upside. However, attention should still be paid to macroeconomic developments and the potential return of tonnage, which may impact the pace of the market going forward. items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report17th April 2026 ATL: FLAT PAC: FIRMER MID EAST: FIRMER Market Comments ATL SHORT OUTLOOK - BOTH THE NORTH AND SOUTH ATLANTIC CONTINUE TO FACE AN OVERHANG OF PPT DELIVERIES, WHICH WILL NEED TO CLEAR EARLY NEXT WEEK IN ORDER TO SUPPORT ANY FURTHER UPSIDE IN RATES. AS IT STANDS, THE MARKET APPEARS TO HAVE FOUND A NEAR-TERM CEILING, AND FURTHER GAINS WILL LIKELY DEPEND ON IMPROVED CARGO VISIBILITY AND A TIGHTENING OF TONNAGE NEXT WEEK. 1A/2A/P6 - 14416/25821/19013 PAC SHORT THE PACIFIC PANAMAX MARKET EXPERIENCED A POSITIVE TRAJECTORY THROUGH THE EARLY AND MID PART OF THE WEEK, BEFORE FLATTENING OFF TOWARDS THE END AT ELEVATED LEVELS WEEK ON WEEK. STRONG COAL-DRIVEN DEMAND, PARTICULARLY FROM INDO AND EAST AUS, SUPPORTED A STEADY BUILD IN CARGO VISIBILITY, WHILE GRAINS PLAYED A MORE SECONDARY BUT STABLE ROLE. ADDITIONALLY, A SLIGHT CORRECTION IN BUNKER PRICES, WHICH CAME OFF FROM RECENT HIGHS, ENCOURAGED CHARTERERS TO MOVE QUICKLY IN COVERING THEIR STEMS EARLIER IN THE WEEK, ADDING TO THE INITIAL SURGE IN ACTIVITY. TONNAGE REMAINED BROADLY BALANCED OVERALL, SLIGHTLY TIGHTER IN THE SOUTH MIDWEEK AND MARGINALLY BUILDING IN THE NORTH HELPING OWNERS MAINTAIN UPWARD PRESSURE ON RATES. AS A RESULT, BOTH P3 AND P5 INDICES TRENDED POSITIVELY THROUGH THE WEEK, SUPPORTED BY ACTIVE FIXING AND IMPROVING SENTIMENT, ALTHOUGH MOMENTUM SLOWED INTO FRIDAY AS FRESH ENQUIRY EASED SLIGHTLY. ON THE FFA SIDE, PAPER HELD A POSITIVE TONE EARLY ON, REFLECTING CONFIDENCE IN NEAR-TERM STRENGTH, BEFORE SOFTENING LATER IN THE WEEK DESPITE A STILL HEALTHY FORWARD CURVE. RATES HAVE GENERALLY RANGED FROM THE HIGH USD 12,000S UP TO USD 14,000 BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS. LEVELS HAVE GRADUALLY BEEN PULLED HIGHER, LARGELY SUPPORTED BY THE FIRMING FRONTHAUL MARKET, WHICH HAS PROVIDED OWNERS WITH GREATER OPTIONALITY AND ALLOWED THEM TO INCREASE OFFERS FOR TA EMPLOYMENT. 2A - GRAIN FRONTHAUL HAS REMAINED THE KEY DRIVING FORCE ACROSS THE ATLANTIC BASIN THIS WEEK. AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED, IT BECAME EVIDENT THAT SEVERAL OPERATORS NEEDED TO COVER PROMPT POSITIONS, WHICH HELPED SUSTAIN UPWARD MOMENTUM. OWNERS WITH SUITABLE FRONTHAUL TONNAGE MAINTAINED FIRM OFFER LEVELS AND WERE GRADUALLY REWARDED, WITH EARLY-WEEK FIXTURES REPORTED IN THE HIGH USD 24,000S AND INDICATIONS OF LOW USD 26,000S BKI EQUIVALENT EX ALGECIRAS BEING FIXED BY CLOSE OF PLAY ON THURSDAY. P6 - A FLURRY OF ACTIVITY AT THE START OF THE WEEK INJECTED MOMENTUM INTO THE P6 MARKET, WITH FIXTURES REPORTED ON TUESDAY AND WEDNESDAY REACHING LEVELS OF UP TO USD 20,000 BKI EQUIVALENT DELIVERY SINGAPORE. HOWEVER, SENTIMENT SHIFTED ON THURSDAY, WITH CHARTERERS STEPPING BACK FROM THE BID SIDE AND ADOPTING A MORE PATIENT APPROACH WHERE CARGO URGENCY ALLOWED. THE WEEK CLOSED ON A SOFTER NOTE, AS THE PPT TONNAGE LIST REMAINS RELATIVELY LONG. MIDWEEK SAW SOME STABILITY WITH GRAINS HOLDING AT REASONABLE LEVELS, BUT THE SECTOR LACKED MOMENTUM COMPARED TO THE MINERALS DRIVEN SOUTHERN MARKETS. BY THE END OF THE WEEK, THERE WAS A SLIGHT UPTICK IN GRAIN INTEREST, THOUGH OVERALL SENTIMENT REMAINED MORE SUBDUED, WITH A SMALL DROP IN AVAILABLE TONNAGE HELPING TO KEEP RATES SUPPORTED DESPITE LIMITED CARGO GROWTH. THE AUSSIE MARKET WAS A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR TO THE WEEK’S STRENGTH, PARTICULARLY THROUGH MIDWEEK WHERE STRONG COAL ENQUIRY INCLUDING JAPANESE TENDERS AND CHINESE DEMAND KEPT PRESSURE ON RATES AND PUSHED FIXTURES HIGHER. HOWEVER, AFTER A BUSY PERIOD, ACTIVITY BEGAN TO TAPER OFF FROM THURSDAY ONWARDS, WITH A NOTICEABLE REDUCTION IN FRESH SPOT DEMAND AND A SHIFT TOWARDS MORE FORWARD DATED CARGOES. BY FRIDAY, EAST AUS COAL, THE KEY DRIVER EARLIER IN THE WEEK, HAD SOFTENED, CONTRIBUTING TO THE OVERALL SLOWDOWN IN RATE MOMENTUM, EVEN AS LEVELS REMAINED ELEVATED. THE INDO MARKET REMAINED CONSISTENTLY ACTIVE THROUGHOUT THE WEEK AND WAS A KEY PILLAR OF SUPPORT FOR THE PACIFIC. STRONG COAL FLOWS INTO CHINA AND INDIA, ALONGSIDE FRESH END-APRIL STEMS, MAINTAINED HEALTHY CARGO VOLUMES AND DROVE COMPETITION AMONG CHARTERERS, PARTICULARLY MIDWEEK WHEN SOME SPOT CARGOES INTO INDIA PAID UP AND OWNERS PUSHED OFFERS HIGHER. EVEN AS THE BROADER MARKET COOLED SLIGHTLY TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, INDO CONTINUED TO PROVIDE A STEADY FLOW OF ENQUIRY, HELPING TO UNDERPIN RATES AND PREVENT ANY SHARP DOWNSIDE. IN CONCLUSION, THE PACIFIC MARKET EXPERIENCED A STRONG, COAL LED RALLY THROUGH MIDWEEK, DRIVEN BY TIGHT TONNAGE AND ROBUST MINERAL DEMAND, BEFORE LOSING MOMENTUM AND STABILIZING AT HIGHER LEVELS. WHILE SENTIMENT HAS TURNED MORE MEASURED, THE OVERALL STRUCTURE OF THE MARKET REMAINS SUPPORTED WITH A RELATIVELY STABLE DEMAND-SUPPLY SETUP IN PLACE Simpson Spence Young Ltd T: +44 (0)20 7977 7400 E: panamax@ssyglobal.comWhile reasonable care has been taken to ensure that the information in this publication is accurate, SSY can accept no responsibility for any errors or omissions or any consequences arising therefrom. Corn exports declined 0.3 Mt on the week to 1.6 Mt, while wheat shipments eased 0.1 Mt to 0.3 Mt. Conversely, shipments of soy (beans+meal) and sorghums each lifted 0.1 Mt to a respective 1.2 Mt and 0.2 Mt. Trading Commentary Cape Another volatile day in the Cape FFA market with Apr and May paid up to highs of 32500 and 35000 respectively. The June range was wide also 33200-34250 while the May v Jun continues to widen and strengthen up to +700. Q2 traded in huge volume up to 33850 during the rally, while activity on the Q3 stalled, trading between 30800 and 31500. The Q3 v Q4 was legged at +100 early in the day with the range on Q4 alone was 30600-30850. Similar to the Q4, the Cals were relatively stable, with 25800-26000 C27 and 23000-23150 C28. PMX Pmx had a quiet start to the day before an afternoon flurry off the back of some macro uncertainty, leaving May trading to highs of 19500. We did find a ceiling and steadily traded back down to just above opening levels. while Jun held a narrow range of 19100 to 19500. Further out, Q3 traded at a low of 18450 and was paid up to 18800, finishing around 18600, while Q4 traded around 17000 and saw some late improvement to 17250. Cal 27 traded around 15000. Overall, it was a steady end to the week, with the market holding firm despite weakness in the wider energy complex. Simpson Spence Young Ltd T: +44 (0)20 7977 |7400 E:snp@ssy.co.uk www.ssyglobal.com 17th April 2026 Source: Baltic Exchange While activity in the Newcastlemax market has remained limited so far this year, this week we report the enbloc sale of sisterships "RTM CARTIER" & "RTM ZHENG HE" (205k dwt, 2012 HHIC - ME Engine) at a price in excess of USD 90 mills to Chinese interests. For readers' reference their sistership, the Ex "MINERAL CLOUDBREAK" (205k dwt, 2012 Hanjin Su- bic), sold in September 2025 at region USD 40 mill to Chinese interests. Turning to the Post -Panamax sector, the "OHSHU MARU" (92k dwt, 2011 Namura) has found new ownership at USD 16.3 mill. Readers will note that her sistership, the Ex "TAIHAKUSAN" (93k dwt, 2009 Namura) , sold in November 2025 at USD 12.5 mill basis SS/DD passed. In the Panamax sector, 2 x sisterships have changed hands, namely the "AOM JULIA" (76k dwt, 2009 Shin Kasado) to Turkish interests & the "ALEXANDROS PETRAKIS" (76k dwt, 2008 Shin Kasado) , both at undisclosed levels. For a point of reference, last month the "AGRI KINSALE" (77k dwt, 2009 Oshima) was sold at low USD 15 mills. Moving to the Ultramax sector, after calling for offers on the 31st of March, we now under- stand that the "ASL IXORA" (61k dwt, 2012 Shin Kasado) has been committed at a price in excess of USD 20 mill. Similarly, her sistership the "AMORE" (61k dwt, 2012 Shin Kasado) has now been sold at USD 20.4 mill to Chinese interests. Readers will note that in January, their sistership the Ex "EXPLORER AFRICA" (61k dwt, 2012 Oshima) sold at low USD 19 mills. In the Supramax sector, after calling for offers on the 14th of April, we now understand that the "SUNNY ROYAL" (58k dwt, 2011 Kawasaki HI) has been sold at USD 18.5 mill to Greek interests. Elsewhere, the "HONOUR" (57k dwt, 2010 COSCO) has found new ownership at a price in excess of USD 13 mill. Additionally, after inviting offers on the 15th of April, clients of Hanson Carriers have been linked to the sale of the "PHOENIX K" (55k dwt, 2007 Oshima - OHBS) at USD 14 mill. In the Handysize sector, the "STRADION" & "DORYSIA " (37k dwt, 2011/2010 HMD) have been committed at USD 25 mill to Vietnamese interests in an enbloc transaction, basis delivery West Africa. Lastly, the "COSCO KUNLUNSHAN" (32k dwt, 2010 Fujian Mawei) has changed hands at USD 8.2 mill. After calling for offers on the 13th of April, we now understand that the "KASAGISAN" (302k dwt, 2006 Mitsui) has been sold at a price in excess of USD 60 mills to Greek interests, a firmer price than that of the "KIHO" (301k dwt, 2006 IHI) , which sold last month at USD 57 mill to clients of Evalend. Moving to the Suezmax sector, clients of Stena have offloaded their "STENA SUR- PRISE" (158k dwt, 2012 Sungdong - Scrubber Fitted) at USD 61 mill to clients of NGM. Read- ers will note that last month the same Sellers sold her sistership, the Ex "STENA SUN- SHINE" (159k dwt, 2013 Samsung HI - ME Engine) , at a price in excess of USD 60 mill to clients of Thenamaris. In the LR2 sector, clients of Trafigura have picked clients of Performance Shipping's DPP trading "P. ALIKI" (105k dwt, 2010 HHI, Epoxy) at USD 42.65 mill basis delivery in Q3 2026 upon completion of her current time charter. Readers will note that her year older ship the "P. SOPHIA" (105k dwt, 2009 HHI, Epoxy) was sold in February at USD 35.65 mill basis delivery in mid 2026. Looking to the LR1 sector, the CPP trading "PAN CAKE" (73k dwt, 2006 Dalian, Epoxy) has been committed at USD 19 mill to Chinese interests basis DD passed, a firmer price than that of her sistership, the "CHEMTRANS TAURUS" (73k dwt, 2006 Dalian, Epoxy) , which was sold in February at USD 12.5 mill. In the MR2 sector, the "OPTIMAL ACE" (50k dwt, 2006 STX, Epoxy - IMO III) has changed hands at a price in excess of USD 16.5 mill basis DD passed. Additionally, the "GT FREE- DOM" (46k dwt, 2003 Shin Kurushima, Epoxy) has been sold at USD 8.5 mill. Concluding this week's second hand tanker news, after inviting offers on the 13th of April, we now understand that the J19 "GINGA SAKER" (20k dwt, 2003 Shin Kurushima, StSt - IMO II/ III / ICE 1C) has been sold at USD 10.8 mill to Chinese interests. Readers will note that earli- er this month her year younger sistership, the "YC AZALEA" (20k dwt, 2004 Shin Kurushima, StSt - IMO II/III) , found new ownership for a similar price at high USD 10 mills. 0102030405060 Jan-22 Apr-22 Jul-22 Oct-22 Jan-23 Apr-23 Jul-23 Oct-23 Jan-24 Apr-24 Jul-24 Oct-24 Jan-25 Apr-25 Jul-25 Oct-25 Jan-26 Apr-26$k/day Cape 180kdwt Cape 182kdwt Panamax 82kdwt Supramax 63kdwt Handysize 38kdwt Sale and Purchase Weekly Market Report BSRA Delivery Bangladesh (US$/LDT) Delivery India (US$/LDT) Tankers (LDT) 30001 & above 475.583 436.000 15001 - 30000 479.083 442.583 7000 - 15000 480.417 444.750 Bulkers (LDT) 20001 & above 464.167 424.917 9001 - 20000 468.500 432.417 5000 - 9000 468.250 434.083 Baltic Recycling Assessments MR Earning (Non -Eco, Non -Scrubber) Source: Baltic Exchange Source: SSY 17th April 2026 There has been a distinct improvement in the volume of enquiry from all the major recycling desti- nations over the past week, which has translated into a notable increase in concluded sales. India has been the primary beneficiary, securing several chemical tanker sales, including one concluded on private terms, all with high quantities of solid stainless steel. When combined with bunkers ROB included in the transactions, these units have generated exceptionally strong price levels. Stolt Tankers have sold the “Stolt Cedar” (11,436 lwt) at a reported level of USD 910 per lwt, and the “Stolt Sea” (8,074 lwt) at a slightly lower level of USD 850 per lwt. Both vessels are understood to contain significant, albeit undisclosed, quantities of stainless steel, and have already arrived, with beaching expected during the upcoming high tides. Sinokor have now concluded the long -anticipated sale of the gas carrier “Hongkong Ener- gy” (31,340 lwt) at a reported level of USD 510 per lwt, on an as is basis in Malaysia. Given the vessel’s extended lay -up history, it is understood that Buyers will proceed with towage rather than reactivation for the delivery voyage, with Bangladesh anticipated to be the final recycling destina- tion. More broadly, domestic steel demand has strengthened across all major markets, providing further support to improving price levels from the waterfront. This firmer demand backdrop, combined with the increasing number of HKC -approved recycling yards, is beginning to add real momentum to competition within the sector, effectively giving the market a much -needed breath of fresh air after a prolonged period of subdued activity. However, despite the recent increase in concluded sales, the overall supply of tonnage remains insufficient to satisfy the full breadth of demand. This is particularly relevant given the number of yards that have invested heavily to achieve HKC compliance, all of whom are now actively seeking to secure units. Newbuilding DSIC (Dalian Shipbuilding Industry Co) have secured tanker orders with deliveries scheduled in 2029 from JP Morgan, Advantage Tankers and Mercuria. JP Morgan has contracted 2+2 units of 307,000 dwt VLCCs, while Advantage Tankers has placed orders for two VLCCs. Mercuria has booked 2+2 VLCCs, in addition to two 115,000 dwt LR2 tankers. Pricing for the VLCCs is estimated at around USD 123 million per unit, while the LR2 tankers are priced at approximately USD 75 million per vessel. DH Shipbuilding in Korea have finalised a contract to construct a 157,000 dwt Suezmax tanker for delivery in July 2029. This was an execution of an option for Laskaridis’ fourth unit, with pricing unchanged at USD 89.2 million. Akrotiri Tankers is understood to have ordered one 157,000 dwt Suezmax tanker at New Times Shipbuilding, with delivery scheduled during 2029. Commercial terms are estimated at approxi- mately USD 82 million per vessel. CSET (COSCO Shipping Energy Transportation) have placed an order for two 75,000 dwt Panamax tankers at COSCO Shipping Offshore Qidong, with deliveries scheduled in Q4 2028, at a contract price of USD 76.5 million per vessel. VOSCO (Vietnam Ocean Shipping JSC) have ordered two 50,000 dwt MR tankers at K Shipbuilding. Commercial details have not been disclosed, though deliveries are expected during 2H 2028, with pricing estimated at up to USD 52 million per vessel. Norse Shipholding is understood to have ordered 4+2 units of 1,800 TEU container vessels, with the firm units split evenly between Fujian Mawei Shipbuilding and Fujian Southeast Shipbuilding. Deliveries are scheduled across 2028, with pricing estimated at approximately USD 32 million per vessel. HD KSOE (Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering) have announced two VLGC contracts this week. Aygas has ordered two 90,000 cbm VLGCs at HD Hyundai Samho, priced at USD 117 million per unit for delivery in Q4 2028 and Q2 2029 respectively. In addition, BGN has contracted four 90,000 cbm VLGCs at HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (Ulsan), priced at USD 114.5 million per ves- sel, with deliveries scheduled by November 2029. ARA Jet Fuel Stocks Fall to Six -Year Low At the Amsterdam -Rotterdam -Antwerp (ARA) storage hub, jet fuel inventories declined by 50KT w -o-w to 600KT during the week end- ing 16 April, the lowest level since April 2020, according to data from Refinitiv.
